summary: Leonard Swidler was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from St. Norbert College, Marquette University, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and the University of Tübingen, later serving as Professor of Catholic Thought and Interreligious Dialogue at Temple University (1966–2022).
Leonard Woolley was a history and archaeology scholar who was educated at St John's School, Leatherhead, and studied at New College from circa 1899 to 1903.
Leonard Zwilling worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and completed his education at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 1976.

Leonard van der Kuijp is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg. He served at the University of Washington (circa 1987–1995) and became Sanskrit and Indian Studies chair at Harvard in 1995.

Leonhard Masing was a linguist who studied under Leo Meyer and August Leskien, attending the University of Tartu, the University of Göttingen, and the University of Leipzig. He subsequently served as a docent (1880–1910) and teacher (1918–1925) at the University of Tartu.

Leonid Kulikov is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences. He held positions at Leiden University, Adam Mickiewicz University, Ghent University, and became a professor at KU Leuven in 2022.

Leonidas Clint was an Indologist who earned an M.A. from Trinity College, Cambridge. He later served as principal at La Martinière College (1845–1854) and Krishnagar Government College (circa 1845–1857).

Leopold Pospisil studied at Charles University, Willamette University, the University of Oregon, and Yale University. He served as a professor at Yale University beginning in 1956 and as an anthropology curator at the Peabody Museum of Natural History (circa 1956–1993).

Leopold von Ranke was a historian who studied at Schulpforta and at the University of Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann. He later held a long-standing academic post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1825 to 1871.

Leopold von Schroeder was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Tartu, Tübingen, and Jena under mentors including Leo Meyer and Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the University of Tartu, University of Innsbruck, and University of Vienna (1899).

Leopoldo de Eguílaz y Yánguas was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his Dr.iuris at Complutense University of Madrid and was appointed Professor of General and Spanish Literature at the University of Granada in 1864.
Lepel Henry Griffin was an Indology and history scholar who was educated at Windlesham House School and Harrow School. He subsequently served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1860 to 1889.

Leslie S. Kawamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his PhD under Herbert V. Guenther at the University of Saskatchewan. He was a professor of Buddhist studies at the University of Calgary from circa 1976 to 2011.
Levi H. Elwell was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Amherst College and Yale University. He served as an instructor in Latin at Amherst College from 1877 to 1878.

Levi McLaughlin is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from the University of Toronto and Princeton University. He has held positions at Kokugakuin University, the University of Iowa, and North Carolina State University (professor from 2012).

Lewin Bentham Bowring was an Indology and history specialist who studied at the East India Company College and Fort William College. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1843–1870) and was Chief Commissioner of the Government of Mysore (circa 1862–1870).

Lewis Doney is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University and SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel. He held posts at the British Museum, NTNU, and Ruhr University Bochum, becoming Professor of Tibetology at Bonn in 2021.

Lewis Hodous was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Case Western Reserve, Hartford Seminary, and Halle-Wittenberg. He headed Fukien Union Theological Seminary (1902–1912, 1914–1917) and was a professor in the Chinese Department at Hartford Seminary (1917–1945).

Lewis Lancaster is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Roanoke College, Claremont School of Theology, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as professor at UC Berkeley and president of University of the West.
Lewis Robert Stacy was a scholar in history and Indology who joined the East India Company in 1804 and served as a lieutenant-colonel in the Bengal Army from circa 1804 to 1848.
